jobs.title: Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
Why This Role

Concourse is building the operating system for State and Local governments. Our platform is a configurable approach to tackling fragmented government data and workflows and turning them into smooth operations for public servants and the constituents they serve. As a Concourse Platform Engineer, you're not building a marginal feature for one product. You're contributing to the infrastructure that scales to our hundreds of products serving millions of Americans.

You own the foundational layer: the data ingestion pipelines, AI workflow orchestration engine, and configurable primitives that support everything above them. Your role is to empower our Forward-Deployed PMs who sit alongside city and county teams, understand their specific workflows, and assemble each agency's solution. A bail management system for a county courthouse. IT Helpdesk for a school district. A water utility operations dashboard. An ERP for a mid-sized city. The FDPMs build those. Your job is to make sure they can.

You're working on the deep infrastructure questions that make every deployment possible: how to reliably ingest data from a 30-year-old mainframe, how to run multi-step AI workflows that government users can audit and trust, how to expose primitives flexible enough to model any government process but constrained enough that non-engineers can build on them.

These are hard, novel problems. The people solving them will define the next generation of government software serving us.

What You'll Do

Design and own the connectors, ingestion pipelines, and data modeling primitives that normalize government data from legacy systems (mainframes, Oracle, flat files, proprietary APIs) into a consistent, queryable foundation
Build the infrastructure for long-running, multi-step AI workflows: task queuing, state management, retries, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and the audit trails government compliance requires
Build and maintain the core primitives FDPMs build on top of: the workflow engine, role-based access model, form and action framework, and event system that let a non-engineer assemble a bail system or permitting platform without writing the plumbing from scratch
Bake in data isolation, access controls, and auditability as core platform features from the start, with a path toward compliance certifications (FedRAMP, CJIS, HIPAA) as we grow
Work directly with the founder on architecture decisions that will compound across every deployment we ever ship

What We're Looking For

A portfolio: what have you built end-to-end, from scratch, under pressure?
Strong backend fluency in Python and/or Node, with solid instincts for data modeling, API design, and building systems that stay reliable and extensible over time
Enough frontend ability to build and reason about a UI, even if you won't own it
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Factory, etc.) as a core part of your daily workflow
Good instincts for abstraction: knowing when to generalize something into a platform primitive vs. when to just ship it
US citizen (required for government work)
Willing to work in-person in Flatiron, NYC (5 days/week)

Nice to have:

Experience building developer platforms or internal tooling, devops/infrastructure, agentic AI orchestration, or work in regulated industries like healthcare, finance, or legal.

About Concourse

Concourse is the fastest-growing govtech, providing software to more than 100 state and local governments across the U.S.

Government calls what we do "IT modernization." We call it a trillion-dollar opportunity to overhaul how government works. Public services are broken not because of bureaucracy but instead because they run on antiquated, user-unfriendly software from legacy vendors.

Some examples: Concourse is powering the legislative management system for one of America's largest cities, a state's entire online bail payment system, and a case-management platform for mental-health response teams.

We are an AI-native company. Our org structure and staffing model are radically different from those of legacy tech companies: we have a flat team of superstar generalists who both own client relationships and manage fleets of long-horizon AI agents.

Our team works together in our Flatiron office five days a week.

Compensation Range: $160K - $200K

jobs.description:
Founding Software Engineer (UX/UI & Systems) - Top 10 Robotics/Hard Tech Startup - Manhattan, NYC - $350k Cash + Founding Equity

We’re hiring for one of NYC’s top 10 robotics startups.
If you’re an elite engineer looking to join a high-density "A " squad - builders from SpaceX, Google, Palantir & Anduril - this
is where you want to be.

Must be based in NYC & role requires US citizenship due to regulatory constraints.

This isn't another abstracted B2B platform or a data-entry dashboard. These guys have fleets of multi-ton autonomous machines deployed globally & we’re hiring Founding Software Engineers
to build the operating system & interface that controls them.

The Team
You will be joining an A squad *-a high-density group of builders from SpaceX, Palantir, Tesla & Google
. We avoid typical corporate friction & process for the sake of process. We hire for high agency, technical depth, & a total lack of ego. As a founding hire, you won't just follow a roadmap-you will define it.

High Autonomy, no micromanagement. You will have the autonomy to own the entire frontend stack from architecture to shipping. You are the bridge between complex robotics telemetry & intuitive operational tools.
Mission Control:
Architecting the UI that handles high-frequency telemetry, 3D spatial data, & real-time fleet management.
Founding Ownership:
You choose the tools, define the architecture, & own the deployment pipeline.
Real Stakes:
You’ll work closely with hardware engineers to ensure our interfaces are as reliable as the machines they control. In this environment, a laggy interface or a confusing UI has real-world consequences.

What we're looking for

Seeking high-signal engineers (we don't care about schools, we care about your aptitude to problem solving) who have seen what to build the best again & again.
Mastery of TypeScript & React:
You understand the internals & how to build for extreme performance & low latency.
Founding Mindset:
You are comfortable with ambiguity & have a bias toward building simple, robust solutions that scale.
High-Signal Pedigree:
You’ve shipped production systems in high-bar environments (SpaceX, Tesla, or similar elite squads).
Product Sense:
You understand how to translate complex system states into intuitive, rock-solid operational tools.

Stack & Comp

Stack:
TypeScript, React, high-performance data visualization.
Location:
NYC (SoHo/Flatiron) - hybrid.
Comp:
$350k - $500k+ base + Founding Member Equity
.

The Process: 1 Week & 0 Take-Homes
We respect your time & move as fast as we ship. Our process is designed to be completed in 1 week:
(Founders) Technical Deep Dive:
A conversation about the architecture of a complex system you’ve built from the ground up.
(Team) Practical Pairing:
Solving a real-world interface or state-management problem together. No Leetcode.
(Exec) Founding Team Chat:
A focus on judgment, trade-offs, & the vision for the product.

If you’re ready to move from building digital-only products to building the interface for the physical world, let’s talk.

TL;DR

Founding Software Engineer (UX/UI & Systems)
Top 10 NYC robotics startup
Software that controls physical systems
Production ownership, real consequences
$350k-$500k+ base + equity
Hybrid - Manhattan, NYC

Equal Opportunity

We're hiring for an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Software Engineer III
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Delivery Engineer is an early-career technical role for engineers and other builders who want to develop broad expertise across technology, customer delivery, and product.

Delivery Engineers are aligned to a state or customer rather than a single product. Working alongside experienced technical and delivery leaders, they develop an end-to-end understanding of how Pearson's platforms, integrations, data flows, and operational processes work together to meet customer requirements and contractual commitments.

This is a hands-on role. Delivery Engineers demonstrate solutions, investigate technical issues, validate integrations, support implementations and production events, and work across teams to drive problems toward resolution. The role provides broad exposure to customers, products, and technology organizations and is designed to develop future leaders across Technology Readiness, Technical Product Management, Product Management, Delivery, Implementation, Support, and Technology.

Key Responsibilities

Develop deep knowledge of assigned state or customer programs, including requirements, contractual commitments, technical solutions, integrations, configurations, and operational processes.

Build and maintain an end-to-end understanding of the customer solution across test administration, test delivery, scoring, reporting, data exchange, identity, infrastructure, and external integrations.

Translate customer, RFP, and contractual requirements into technical requirements, solution approaches, validation criteria, and delivery considerations.

Create and maintain system diagrams, integration flows, data flows, and other technical documentation that clearly explains how the customer solution works.

Develop the product and solution knowledge needed to confidently explain and demonstrate Pearson's technology capabilities to customers and internal stakeholders.

Participate in customer technical discussions, demonstrations, integration reviews, solution workshops, and RFP or proposal activities.

Provide hands-on technical support during implementation, integration testing, readiness activities, administration windows, production events, and customer escalations.

Investigate technical issues across systems by analyzing configurations, APIs, integrations, data flows, logs, and system behavior.

Partner across Engineering, Product, Quality Engineering, Implementation, Operations, Support, Security, and Infrastructure to resolve technical issues and delivery risks.

Support end-to-end validation to ensure systems, integrations, and operational processes collectively meet customer requirements and commitments.

Identify technical gaps, dependencies, risks, and product limitations, and help ensure they are understood and addressed by the appropriate teams.

Apply lessons from implementations, incidents, and customer feedback to improve products, documentation, processes, and future customer solutions.

Required Qualifications

1 to 3 years of experience in software engineering, systems engineering, technical support, quality engineering, or another hands-on technology discipline, or equivalent experience building, testing, integrating, or operating software systems.

Practical experience with software applications, APIs, integrations, data flows, cloud-based systems, or related enterprise technologies.

Experience troubleshooting technical issues using structured problem-solving and technical evidence.

Ability to read technical documentation and create or interpret system diagrams, integration flows, and data flows.

Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Strong technical curiosity, problem-solving skills, and interest in understanding how complex systems work together.

Ability to collaborate across technical, product, implementation, and operational teams.

Interest in working directly with customers and developing confidence in customer-facing technical discussions and demonstrations.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with APIs, cloud platforms, identity and access management, logging and monitoring tools, or distributed applications.

Experience supporting customer implementations, integration testing, production systems, incident response, or technical escalations.

Experience in enterprise technology, education technology, government, or large-scale assessment.

Exposure to RFPs, proposals, product management, solution engineering, implementation, or delivery functions.

What Makes Someone Successful in This Role

Successful Delivery Engineers are curious, hands-on problem solvers who want to understand both the customer and the technology. They communicate clearly, collaborate effectively across teams, ask thoughtful questions, surface risks, and stay engaged until problems are resolved.

They are comfortable learning beyond a single application and are motivated to understand how multiple products and integrations come together as one customer solution.

Career Development

The Delivery Engineer role is intentionally designed as a development path for early-career technical talent. Through direct exposure to customers, products, engineering teams, implementations, and production delivery, Delivery Engineers build the technical judgment, product understanding, and customer perspective needed for future opportunities in Technology Readiness, Technical Product Management, Product Management, Delivery, Implementation, Support, Solution Engineering, and broader Technology leadership.

Delivery Engineers build depth on the customer and breadth across the technology ecosystem.

Compensation at Pearson is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and specific location. As required by the California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York State, New York City, Vermont, Washington State, and Washington DC laws, the pay range for this position is as follows:

The minimum full-time salary range is between $80,000 - $120,000.

This position is eligible to participate in an annual incentive program, and information on benefits offered is here.

Applications will be accepted through 16th November 2026. This window may be extended depending on business needs.

Who we are:

At Pearson, our purpose is simple: to help people realize the life they imagine through learning. We believe that every learning opportunity is a chance for a personal breakthrough. We are the world's lifelong learning company. For us, learning isn't just what we do. It's who we are. To learn more: We are Pearson.

Pearson is an Equal Opportunity Employer and a member of E-Verify. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit and business need. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status or any other group protected by law. We actively seek qualified candidates who are protected veterans and individuals with disabilities as defined under VEVRAA and Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act.

If you are an individual with a disability and are unable or limited in your ability to use or access our career site as a result of your disability, you may request reasonable accommodations by emailing TalentExperienceGlobalTeam@grp.pearson.com.

new_jobs.title: Software Engineer III
new_jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Delivery Engineer is an early-career technical role for engineers and other builders who want to develop broad expertise across technology, customer delivery, and product.

Delivery Engineers are aligned to a state or customer rather than a single product. Working alongside experienced technical and delivery leaders, they develop an end-to-end understanding of how Pearson's platforms, integrations, data flows, and operational processes work together to meet customer requirements and contractual commitments.

This is a hands-on role. Delivery Engineers demonstrate solutions, investigate technical issues, validate integrations, support implementations and production events, and work across teams to drive problems toward resolution. The role provides broad exposure to customers, products, and technology organizations and is designed to develop future leaders across Technology Readiness, Technical Product Management, Product Management, Delivery, Implementation, Support, and Technology.

Key Responsibilities

Develop deep knowledge of assigned state or customer programs, including requirements, contractual commitments, technical solutions, integrations, configurations, and operational processes.

Build and maintain an end-to-end understanding of the customer solution across test administration, test delivery, scoring, reporting, data exchange, identity, infrastructure, and external integrations.

Translate customer, RFP, and contractual requirements into technical requirements, solution approaches, validation criteria, and delivery considerations.

Create and maintain system diagrams, integration flows, data flows, and other technical documentation that clearly explains how the customer solution works.

Develop the product and solution knowledge needed to confidently explain and demonstrate Pearson's technology capabilities to customers and internal stakeholders.

Participate in customer technical discussions, demonstrations, integration reviews, solution workshops, and RFP or proposal activities.

Provide hands-on technical support during implementation, integration testing, readiness activities, administration windows, production events, and customer escalations.

Investigate technical issues across systems by analyzing configurations, APIs, integrations, data flows, logs, and system behavior.

Partner across Engineering, Product, Quality Engineering, Implementation, Operations, Support, Security, and Infrastructure to resolve technical issues and delivery risks.

Support end-to-end validation to ensure systems, integrations, and operational processes collectively meet customer requirements and commitments.

Identify technical gaps, dependencies, risks, and product limitations, and help ensure they are understood and addressed by the appropriate teams.

Apply lessons from implementations, incidents, and customer feedback to improve products, documentation, processes, and future customer solutions.

Required Qualifications

1 to 3 years of experience in software engineering, systems engineering, technical support, quality engineering, or another hands-on technology discipline, or equivalent experience building, testing, integrating, or operating software systems.

Practical experience with software applications, APIs, integrations, data flows, cloud-based systems, or related enterprise technologies.

Experience troubleshooting technical issues using structured problem-solving and technical evidence.

Ability to read technical documentation and create or interpret system diagrams, integration flows, and data flows.

Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Strong technical curiosity, problem-solving skills, and interest in understanding how complex systems work together.

Ability to collaborate across technical, product, implementation, and operational teams.

Interest in working directly with customers and developing confidence in customer-facing technical discussions and demonstrations.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with APIs, cloud platforms, identity and access management, logging and monitoring tools, or distributed applications.

Experience supporting customer implementations, integration testing, production systems, incident response, or technical escalations.

Experience in enterprise technology, education technology, government, or large-scale assessment.

Exposure to RFPs, proposals, product management, solution engineering, implementation, or delivery functions.

What Makes Someone Successful in This Role

Successful Delivery Engineers are curious, hands-on problem solvers who want to understand both the customer and the technology. They communicate clearly, collaborate effectively across teams, ask thoughtful questions, surface risks, and stay engaged until problems are resolved.

They are comfortable learning beyond a single application and are motivated to understand how multiple products and integrations come together as one customer solution.

Career Development

The Delivery Engineer role is intentionally designed as a development path for early-career technical talent. Through direct exposure to customers, products, engineering teams, implementations, and production delivery, Delivery Engineers build the technical judgment, product understanding, and customer perspective needed for future opportunities in Technology Readiness, Technical Product Management, Product Management, Delivery, Implementation, Support, Solution Engineering, and broader Technology leadership.

Delivery Engineers build depth on the customer and breadth across the technology ecosystem.

Compensation at Pearson is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and specific location. As required by the California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York State, New York City, Vermont, Washington State, and Washington DC laws, the pay range for this position is as follows:

The minimum full-time salary range is between $80,000 - $120,000.

This position is eligible to participate in an annual incentive program, and information on benefits offered is here.

Applications will be accepted through 16th November 2026. This window may be extended depending on business needs.

Who we are:

At Pearson, our purpose is simple: to help people realize the life they imagine through learning. We believe that every learning opportunity is a chance for a personal breakthrough. We are the world's lifelong learning company. For us, learning isn't just what we do. It's who we are. To learn more: We are Pearson.
